Valmiki reserve reports rise in tiger count

The Valmiki Tiger Reserve has reported an increase in its big cat population, with the latest camera-trap exercise estimating 56 tigers against 41 in the previous cycle.

Forest officials credited inviolate grassland management, reduced biotic pressure and a growing prey base for the improvement.

The reserve, spread across West Champaran along the Nepal border, is the state's only tiger habitat and a key link in the Terai Arc landscape.

Conservationists cautioned that dispersing tigers increasingly stray into farmland, and sought faster compensation for cattle kills and crop damage.

The department said three new anti-poaching camps and a rapid response unit would be operational before winter.
